articles.title: You Do Not Find Your Purpose. You Build It
articles.titleHinglish: Purpose Milta Nahi Hai, Banaya Jaata Hai
articles.content:
The way purpose is usually described sets people up to fail. It is presented as a hidden object — something you already have, waiting to be discovered, and until you find it your life is a placeholder. So people sit and wait for a feeling of certainty that, for most, never arrives.

A more accurate description: purpose is built out of what you actually do, and it usually becomes visible in hindsight rather than in advance.

Most people who look purposeful did not begin that way. They started something ordinary, got slightly good at it, found that being useful was satisfying, went deeper, and at some point the thing became meaningful because of the investment rather than before it. Meaning follows commitment far more often than it precedes it.

This is why the advice to find your passion first fails so many people. Passion is generally a result of competence. You rarely love what you are bad at, and almost everyone is bad at everything for the first year.

A few practical replacements for the search.

Ask what you are willing to be useful for. Purpose that is entirely about self-expression tends to feel thin. Almost everyone who describes their work as meaningful can name a specific person or group who is better off because of it. That is not sentimental; it is the most common structure of a meaningful life.

Notice what you do when nobody is paying you. Not hobbies exactly — what you read about, argue about, cannot stop fixing. That is data.

Run experiments instead of deliberating. A month of doing something teaches you more than a year of considering it. Most people try to think their way to certainty, which is exactly the tool that does not work here.

And allow purpose to be small and plural. A life can be meaningful because of the way you raise a child, the reliability you bring to unglamorous work, and the people you look after — all at once, with no grand mission statement anywhere. The requirement that it be one large calling is a modern invention, and it makes many perfectly good lives feel like failures.

One honest note for a hard period. If you are in a stretch where you feel nothing means anything, that is often not a purpose problem. Exhaustion, grief and depression all produce that exact symptom, and they do not respond to career reflection. Rest first, and get help if it persists. Meaning tends to return on its own once the body and the mind are not running on empty — and if it does not, that is a signal worth taking to someone qualified.
articles.contentHinglish:
Purpose ko jis tarah samjhaya jaata hai wo logon ko fail hone ke liye taiyaar karta hai. Use ek chhupi hui cheez ki tarah rakha jaata hai — kuch jo aapke paas pehle se hai, milne ka intezaar kar raha hai, aur jab tak wo na mile aapki zindagi bas jagah bhar rahi hai. Isliye log us yakeen ki feeling ka intezaar karte baithe rehte hain jo zyadatar logon ko kabhi aati hi nahi.

Zyada sahi varnan: purpose usi se banta hai jo aap sach mein karte ho, aur wo aksar peeche mud kar dikhta hai, pehle se nahi.

Jo log purposeful dikhte hain unme se zyadatar ne aise shuru nahi kiya tha. Unhone kuch aam shuru kiya, usme thode achhe hue, paaya ki kaam ka hona santosh deta hai, aur gehre gaye — aur kisi mod par wo cheez arthpurn ban gayi, uss nivesh ki wajah se, uss se pehle nahi. Arth pratibaddhata ke peechhe aata hai, aage se kahin zyada baar.

Isiliye "pehle apna passion dhoondho" wali salaah itne logon ko fail karti hai. Passion aam taur par kaabiliyat ka nateeja hai. Jisme aap bure ho usse pyaar shayad hi hota hai, aur lagbhag har koi har cheez mein pehle saal bura hi hota hai.

Talaash ki jagah kuch practical cheezein.

Poochho ki aap kis cheez ke liye kaam ke banna chahte ho. Wo purpose jo poori tarah apni abhivyakti ka hai wo aksar patla lagta hai. Jo bhi apne kaam ko arthpurn batata hai wo lagbhag hamesha koi khaas insaan ya group bata sakta hai jinka uski wajah se bhala hua. Yeh bhavukta nahi hai; arthpurn zindagi ki sabse aam banawat yahi hai.

Gaur karo ki jab koi paisa nahi de raha tab aap karte kya ho. Bilkul hobby nahi — wo jiske baare mein aap padhte ho, bahas karte ho, jise theek karne se ruk nahi paate. Wo data hai.

Sochne ki jagah experiment karo. Ek mahina kuch karna ek saal usi ke baare mein sochne se zyada sikhata hai. Zyadatar log yakeen tak soch kar pahunchna chahte hain, aur theek yahi auzaar yahan kaam nahi karta.

Aur purpose ko chhota aur ek se zyada hone do. Ek zindagi isliye arthpurn ho sakti hai ki aapne bachche ko kaise paala, aap bina chamak wale kaam mein kitne bharosemand ho, aur aap kin logon ka khayal rakhte ho — sab ek saath, bina kisi bade mission statement ke. Yeh shart ki wo ek hi badi pukaar ho, aaj ki ijaad hai, aur wo bahut si bilkul theek zindagiyon ko asafalta jaisa mehsoos karwati hai.

Ek imaandaar baat mushkil daur ke liye. Agar aap us daur mein ho jahan kuch bhi arthpurn nahi lagta, to aksar wo purpose ki problem hoti hi nahi. Thakan, gham aur depression — teeno theek yahi lakshan banate hain, aur wo career par soch-vichaar se theek nahi hote. Pehle aaram karo, aur agar yeh bana rahe to madad lo. Arth aksar khud lautta hai jab sharir aur dimaag khaali par nahi chal rahe hote — aur agar nahi lautta, to wo signal kisi qualified insaan tak le jaane laayak hai.

articles.title: An Ordinary Life Is Not a Failed One
articles.titleHinglish: Ek Saadi Zindagi Fail Hui Zindagi Nahi Hai
articles.content:
There is a quiet cruelty in the culture of the last twenty years. Everyone is told they are meant for something extraordinary, that they should build, scale, disrupt, be remembered. It sounds generous. In practice it has made an entire generation feel that a decent job, a small home, a few good relationships and a quiet Sunday constitute a failure.

Most lives are ordinary. That is a statistical fact, not an insult. And the people in them are not less happy — often they are considerably more so than the ones performing significance.

It is worth checking who benefits from the pressure. The message that you must always be more is sold alongside courses, apps, and subscriptions. Restlessness is a market, and contentment does not convert well.

Some things that get lost in the noise.

A life is mostly made of hours, not milestones. The trip, the promotion and the wedding occupy a handful of days. The rest is breakfast, commuting, conversations, small tasks and evenings. A life optimised for peak achievements and unpleasant on ordinary Tuesdays is a bad trade, and it is the most common one.

Being dependable is not a small thing. Most of what holds a family, a neighbourhood or an office together is unremarkable people doing unremarkable things reliably. That work is invisible precisely because it works, and the people doing it are not lesser participants in life.

And nobody is keeping the score you are imagining. You are competing in a tournament that has no organisers, no audience and no prize, against people who are mostly worried about their own standing.

One fair caveat, because this argument can be misused. This is not a case for staying somewhere that is making you miserable, and it is not permission to stop trying. Ambition is fine. Wanting more is fine. The point is only that greatness is not the entry fee for a life worth living, and treating it that way makes people miserable in situations that are, by any honest measure, good.

The test is simple and personal. Ask what you would want your life to have contained, at the end. Almost nobody answers with rank or revenue. Most answers are about people, a few things done well, and having been present for them. That answer is available to almost anyone, starting from wherever they currently are.
articles.contentHinglish:
Pichhle bees saal ki culture mein ek khamosh kathorta hai. Har kisi ko bola jaata hai ki wo kisi asaadharan cheez ke liye bana hai, ki use banana chahiye, scale karna chahiye, disrupt karna chahiye, yaad rakha jaana chahiye. Sunne mein dariyadil lagta hai. Asal mein isne ek poori peedhi ko yeh mehsoos karwaya hai ki ek theek job, chhota ghar, kuch achhe rishte aur ek shaant Sunday — yeh asafalta hai.

Zyadatar zindagiyan aam hoti hain. Yeh ek aankda hai, taana nahi. Aur unme rehne wale log kam khush nahi hote — aksar wo un logon se kaafi zyada khush hote hain jo mahaanata ka performance kar rahe hain.

Yeh dekhna zaroori hai ki is dabaav se faayda kiska hai. "Tumhe hamesha aur zyada banna hai" wala sandesh courses, apps aur subscriptions ke saath becha jaata hai. Bechaini ek market hai, aur santosh achha convert nahi karta.

Shor mein kuch cheezein kho jaati hain.

Zindagi zyadatar ghanton se banti hai, milestones se nahi. Wo trip, wo promotion, wo shaadi — kuch ginne-chune din ghera karte hain. Baaki sab nashta, safar, baat-cheet, chhote kaam aur shaamein hai. Wo zindagi jo sabse oonche lamhon ke liye optimise ki gayi ho aur aam Mangalvaar ko bhaddhi ho — wo bura sauda hai, aur sabse aam sauda bhi.

Bharosemand hona chhoti baat nahi hai. Parivaar, mohalla ya office ko jodne wala zyadatar hissa aise saadaran log hain jo saadaran kaam bharose se karte hain. Wo kaam isliye anadekha rehta hai kyunki wo chalta hai, aur usse karne wale zindagi ke chhote hissedaar nahi hain.

Aur jis scoreboard ki aap kalpana kar rahe ho use koi nahi bhar raha. Aap us tournament mein khel rahe ho jiske na organiser hain, na audience, na inaam — aur saamne wale zyadatar apni hi jagah ki chinta mein hain.

Ek imaandaar baat, kyunki is dalil ka galat istemaal ho sakta hai. Yeh us jagah rukne ki dalil nahi hai jo aapko dukhi kar rahi hai, aur na hi koshish chhod dene ki ijazat. Mahatvakanksha theek hai. Zyada chahna theek hai. Baat sirf itni hai ki jeene laayak zindagi ki entry fee mahaanata nahi hai, aur use fee maan lena logon ko un haalaton mein dukhi kar deta hai jo kisi bhi imaandaar paimane se achhe hain.

Test simple aur niji hai. Poochho ki ant mein aap chahoge ki aapki zindagi mein kya raha ho. Lagbhag koi rank ya revenue nahi bolta. Zyadatar jawab logon ke baare mein hote hain, kuch cheezein jo theek se ki gayi, aur unme maujood hone ke baare mein. Wo jawab lagbhag har kisi ke liye maujood hai, wahan se shuru karke jahan wo abhi hai.
